title: Adam Schiff addresses copyright protection, higher education policy, and wildfire response
text:

U.S. Rep. Adam Schiff Representing California's 30th Congressional District | Facebook Website
Adam Schiff, U.S. Congressman representing California’s 30th district since 2001 and a Harvard alumnus, has recently addressed issues ranging from intellectual property rights to higher education and emergency response efforts in his latest social media posts.
On August 5, 2025, Schiff announced legislative collaboration with Senator Thom Tillis on protecting artists’ rights. He stated, "Every artist and creator deserves to be compensated for their talent. As leading members on the Judiciary Subcommittee on Intellectual Property, @SenThomTillis and I are partnering on a new bill that gives our courts the power to protect American artists from foreign piracy."
Later the same day, Schiff commented on ongoing debates concerning academic independence at Harvard University. He wrote, "Harvard has stood firm against Trump’s war on higher education. That needs to continue. I’m joining other Harvard alumni in Congress to urge the university not to capitulate. You can’t make a good faith deal with an administration that is not acting in good faith." This message reflects Schiff's connection as a Harvard graduate; he earned his JD from Harvard University in 1985 after graduating from Stanford University in 1982.
On August 6, 2025, Schiff expressed appreciation for emergency personnel responding to wildfires in California. He posted, "Grateful to all the first responders working hard to battle the #GiffordFire in Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. I’ve been in touch with local officials to make sure they are receiving every resource necessary to aid in containment and recovery efforts."
Schiff has served continuously in Congress since replacing James E. Rogan in 2001 after serving four years in the California Senate. Born in Framingham, Massachusetts, Schiff currently resides in Burbank.
